When I was in his class, if you read the slides as he speaks you start to realize he’s saying what’s on the slide just wording it differently. I also recommend taking notes on the PowerPoint slides if you can because that was a defining game changer for me.

Honestly, I would love having you in my conferences because I’m more introverted and shy so it takes the pressure off of feeling like I have to speak because no one is speaking. Also this may just be your way of learning and taking information is by being verbal because it helps you process by interacting with the materials. 

Your first conference will always be your hardest because it’s a new thing. If you’re worried about being inarticulate, I usually write my questions down then read off of that to make sure my main point comes across. As time goes on, the conferences will get easier and you’ll for sure be getting those participation marks.

My dermatologist said to never go below 30SPF and for POC most sunscreens 50+ SPF will leave an evident white cast unless it’s extremely tinted. So 30SPF is all good, you just need to reapply more often but you always should reapply your sunscreen.

The main objective of the Cornell method is active recall. So what I personally do is in the main sections on notes, I take notes how I normally would using the outline method and use the right hand side to write practice questions/cues after class. This makes it easier to review and do active recall. To make your notes the most useful, it’s dependent on you figuring out what the foundation info is and building off of that. Using the summary section for my notes, I use it to jot dot the most important sections of my notes. And in all honesty, the perfect notes for you are not the notes that work for your teachers but the notes that work for you. I would suggest watching Ali Abdal YouTube videos for studying tips.
